blocks.text: Status: CANONICAL — GENERAL-ENGLISH GATE MAY BEGIN

Controlled English is now an executable, deliberately restricted input language. It is not unrestricted prose. It accepts exact quoted canonical atom or approved compound labels, an explicit runtime state, and documented uppercase grammar keywords. Unicode NFC, case-insensitive label lookup, and collapsed internal whitespace normalize input without changing the selected canonical target.

The compiler never infers synonyms, pronouns, omitted roles, tense, scope, or a preferred reading. Unknown labels, labels routed only to grammar, Semantic IR, or a documented gap, ambiguous labels, malformed syntax, and underspecified slotted compounds return a structured error and no partial IR.

Every statement ends with one period and begins with ASSERT, QUESTION, COMMAND, DEFINE, or POSSIBILITY. A lexical occurrence is written as a quoted controlled label followed by [0], [1], or [2]. num remains the fixed name of runtime state 2 in rendering; it is not accepted as a numeric or fourth state.

The simple template supports ordered NOT, MODAL, and ASPECT operators; typed ROLE arguments; TIME relations to SPEECH_TIME; MEASURE with canonical decimal and unit; and QUANTIFIER. Separate unambiguous templates support SEQUENCE with THEN, PARALLEL with AND, finite REPEAT … TIMES, and IF … THEN conditionals. Each construct maps to its corresponding canonical Semantic-IR node and edge types.

All 324 canonical atom labels and 28 approved compound labels are available, for 352 deterministic controlled lexical routes. An approved compound with open slots must use the simple template and bind every slot with its named ROLE. The directed data-link template therefore requires explicit source and target arguments. Runtime state, negation, modality, aspect, time, and lexical trits remain independent dimensions.

The dedicated compiler validator passes 13 of 13 checks. It includes 16 golden successful constructions and 17 negative cases with stable error codes. It also compiles, renders, and inverse-decodes all 352 controlled labels; checks exact target identity and deterministic repeated output; verifies structured errors contain no Semantic IR; and confirms open-slot enforcement. The complete project regression passes with every prior authority layer unchanged.

This release changes no atom, generated form, compound, sense route, or etymology. Controlled English may now be used as the safe translation interface to canonical Semantic IR and EZF-1. General English is the next authorized gate. It must produce ranked candidate IRs with evidence and confidence, request clarification when ambiguity is material, and never silently choose the first matching sense. Glyph and audio generation remain later work.
